rationale: A is more decision-useful because it lays out the live alternatives explicitly, recommends a staged path, and gives a concrete near-term sequence: incident review, hardening sprint, reassessment, then partial rewrite if warranted. It handles uncertainty better by tying the choice to incident concentration and architectural evidence, not just a general anti-rewrite stance. B is strong and adds a useful escalation trigger plus a modest quantitative element (15–20%, X incidents/month), but it is less discriminative among options and less explicit about when to choose partial rewrite versus stabilization only. A better supports a careful decision-maker facing real tradeoffs.
